Installing Familiar on a Mac
============================

1. Drag Familiar into the Applications folder (in this window).

2. Open Familiar from Applications. It isn't notarized by Apple yet, so macOS says it
   can't verify the app: click Done (not Move to Trash).

3. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security, and next to
   "Familiar was blocked" click Open Anyway. Confirm with your password or Touch ID,
   then click Open. (On macOS 14 or earlier, Control-click Familiar in Applications,
   choose Open, then Open again.)

4. If macOS says Familiar "is damaged and can't be opened", open Terminal and run:

       xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Familiar.app

   then open Familiar again.

You only do this once. Familiar keeps working from the menu bar when its window is closed;
quit it from there or with Command-Q.

You also need:
- Claude Code, installed and signed in: in Terminal run
      npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
  (or: brew install --cask claude-code), then run "claude" once to sign in.
- Node.js 20 or later (https://nodejs.org or "brew install node").
- Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge, for the browser tool.

The first launch downloads Familiar's built-in database once (internet needed).
Your data lives in the .familiar folder in your home folder.
